text:
ria: Quick FYI — while onboarding aurora-v2q we hit a reproducible structured-output mis-serialization where arrays become newline-delimited object maps (ndjson-like) and our strict parser fails. Not high qps but very consistent on a couple templates.

omar: Can you paste a small example?

ria: Simple repro from canary logs:

Expected (array):
{"steps":[{"op":"lookup","id":1},{"op":"apply","id":2}]}

Observed (ndjson-ish / map):
{"steps":{"0":{"op":"lookup","id":1}}
{"1":{"op":"apply","id":2}}

Note: we see a JSON object then a newline then another object — total payload is technically multiple JSON docs glued together.

jin: That will blow up our validator (we expect a single JSON doc with an array). Is this only in 2-bit quant?

ria: Canary snapshot: aurora-v2q (int8) multijson_rate: 1.8% last 12h; aurora-fp16: 0.02%. Triggered primarily on long step lists and when streaming with chunked flushes.

kb-bot: alert: eng-ml.multijson_rate > 1% for 1h -> @eng-ml on-call

omar: Hypothesis: streaming flushes + quantization noise cause the emitter to flush partial objects then continue, producing separate JSON objects instead of wrapping in array brackets. Two mitigation tracks: parser-collector that concatenates multi-doc payloads into a single array, or runtime enforcement to always start array bracket and keep stateful streaming tokens until closing bracket.

jin: Parser-collector sounds lower-risk: rule = if top-level key is expected to be array and payload looks like N JSON docs each with numeric-indexed object, concat into array preserving numeric order and gaps. But we must detect ndjson vs intentionally multiple-doc responses.

ria: I ran a replay on 1200 canary failures: simple concat would have fixed ~61% of cases and kept clear failure signals for truly malformed outputs. False-repair rate in spot-check was 1.5%.

omar: For safety: implement parser-collector behind feature flag + header X-Structured-Collect: concat(ndjson->array). Add telemetry fields: collected_count, collection_confidence, and store raw multiform pairs to s3://eng-ml/quarantine/multijson for auditing (200/h).

jin: Also add a runtime knob to prefer less aggressive flush when streaming for tool-heavy prompts. Platform team might want to expose a per-route streaming policy.

ria: Short rollout plan:
- PR for collector + unit tests for ndjson->array conversion (jin)
- Bench to quantify correlation with batch_size & streaming chunk size (omar)
- Ship behind flag to 3% canary, monitor collected_count vs parse_fail_rate and downstream tool success.

omar: I'll run eval-suite with tags: batch_size, stream_chunk_size, quant profile. Command:
``
eval-runner --model aurora-v2q --quant int8 --suite multijson-suite --samples 6000 --tags batch_size,stream_chunk_size --out /tmp/aurora_multijson.jsonl
``

kb-bot: deploy planned: aurora-v2q collector-flag -> 3% at 2026-03-26T14:00Z by @ria

jin: One more safety: if collector sees non-consecutive numeric indices or mixed keys, do NOT auto-collect; instead surface example to quarantine and increment noncollectable_count. This avoids accidental reordering.

ria: Agreed. Also add header X-Structured-Repair: collected(steps) when applied so clients can opt for strict mode if they prefer.

omar: If eval shows flux correlated with stream_chunk_size, platform can reduce default chunking for tool-heavy routes. I'll tag platform in the follow-up.

jin: I'll open the PR and add tests for ndjson-bytes boundary cases + UTF-8 partial sequences.

ria: Thanks team. If this safely reduces end-user retries it buys a lot of reliability for tool-based flows.

deploy-bot: canary: aurora-v2q collector-flag v1 scheduled 2026-03-26T14:00Z -> 3% by @ria
